name: messenger-chat-flow
title: Messenger Chat Flow
description: A scripted messaging conversation with delivery details: timestamps and read ticks or a delivered receipt, a typing status in the header, a send button that morphs from mic to send, typing dots and reactions that pop onto bubbles.
useWhen: A scene needs a messaging conversation with delivery details (timestamps, ticks, a delivered receipt) without naming a messenger.
The whole beat should be scripted from a messages list: outgoing text types into the composer, dots precede replies, reactions pop in.
A customer-chat or notification story wants the header to flip between online and typing.
avoidWhen: You only need the bare conversation without receipts: use chat-flow.
You only need one message landing on a beat you time yourself: use message-bubble.
The video must read as a specific messenger with its own chrome.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Messages
variables.description: JSON array of {"from":"me"|"them","text","reaction","time"}; reaction and time are optional. Three short messages fit the 12 second default; lengthen the clip for more.
variables.default: [{"from": "me", "text": "Hey — ready for the demo?", "time": "9:40"}, {"from": "them", "text": "Yep, pushing it live now", "reaction": "🔥", "time": "9:41"}, {"from": "me", "text": "Perfect, sending the link over", "reaction": "👍", "time": "9:41"}]

variables.label: Contact name
variables.description: Name in the header and on the avatar next to replies. Leave empty to show "Chat".

variables.label: Style
variables.description: Ticks: timestamps and read ticks, typing status in the header, mic-to-send button. Receipt: centered header, a Delivered line under the last message, a field with an inline send button.

variables.label: Accent
variables.description: Colour of outgoing bubbles, the send button and the online status.

variables.label: Transparent
variables.description: Leave the background clear so the conversation sits over your own scene.

variables.label: Speed
variables.description: Playback speed of the scripted interaction. 2 plays it twice as fast and holds the end.
